results.title: Watch: Delhi Police suspends ACP for ‘violation of discipline’ after protest by 100 personnel
results.content: Delhi Police ACP Manasvi Vashishta, who led a protest by police personnel against the transfer of two officers following a scuffle at Shahdara police station, has been suspended for “violation of discipline”. Around 100 personnel had gathered outside police headquarters on November 2, demanding the reinstatement of Vashishta and SHO Arun Kumar. The protesters also raised five demands, including clear guidelines for handling confrontations involving lawyers and action against lawyers allegedly involved in misconduct.

results.title: Watch: Delhi firecracker traders face stock challenges after Supreme Court relaxes ban
results.content: The Supreme Court has allowed green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8, but environmental activists have raised concerns over poor enforcement and rising pollution. While traders say the short notice has left them with little time to arrange stocks, Delhi Police have announced restrictions on the sale and use of firecrackers. A firecracker fair in Siliguri is also selling only NEDFI-certified green crackers, with safety measures in place.

results.title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence: Who sets the rules? | The Hindu Explains
results.content: The debate on how to regulate artificial intelligence is intensifying worldwide. From safety guardrails and algorithmic accountability to cyber risks highlighted by CERT-In and the growing divide between tech superpowers and the Global South, regulating AI has become one of the defining challenges of our time. In this deep-dive explainer, The Hindu talks to DR. S. Gokul Krishnan, Research Director at the Centre For Responsible AI, IIT Madras, and Suhail Nathani, Managing Partner, Economic Laws Practice, to understand the major hurdles of AI governance, the limits of self-regulation, and what India and other nations must do to build safe, resilient, and native AI ecosystems.
